## Specific task description

Task instruction: Open the cabinet with smooth finish's drawer and set the small rounded plastic mouse inside with the other arm.

Task description: Open the drawer of the smooth, light-wood cabinet in the center and put the rounded gray-green plastic mouse at the front left of the table inside. The right arm operates the drawer this round; the left arm picks up and places the mouse.

Success criteria: The mouse is inside the open drawer, close to the designated placement point in both left-right and front-back directions. It is slightly higher than its initial tabletop position and within the drawer storage range near the table. The left gripper is open and has released it.

## Execution tips

- When grasping the horizontal handle, choose its middle away from the end supports, effectively surround it from above and below, and avoid the cabinet face. Pull smoothly toward the cabinet front along the drawer slide direction to reduce slipping or lateral jamming.
- Grip broad middle sections of the mouse sides, contacting sidewalls rather than only its domed top or narrow ends. Open slightly wider than the grasp section and confirm the fingers surround the body before closing.
- As the left arm approaches the drawer opening, keep the right arm sufficiently open and leave room at the entry to prevent the drawer from sliding shut on the mouse or fingers.
- During transport, leave clearance from the tall bottle to the left of the cabinet. Before entering the drawer, confirm the mouse base and fingers can both clear the front panel's upper edge, so the object does not pass over while the fingers remain caught on the edge.
- Release only after the mouse is supported by the drawer bottom, then withdraw the fingers through the available space to reduce the risk of the rounded shell sliding or being pulled out by the gripper.
